strengths: The per-orientation accuracy analysis reveals structure hidden by average OoD accuracy. This is an interesting empirical contribution for researchers studying viewpoint robustness and learned invariances.

The fully-seen/restricted-seen design provides useful experimental control. Keeping training-set size constant and evaluating the same restricted instances while varying instance diversity strengthens the interpretation of the diversity results.

The experiments cover four architectures, multiple object categories, five orientation distributions, and controls involving augmentation, pretraining, training-set size, and scale. Three trials with confidence intervals support the main comparisons.

The object images overlaid on accuracy heatmaps communicate the observed patterns effectively. The small-angle and in-plane components provide an understandable, testable characterization of those patterns.
weaknesses: Necessary claim revision: The abstract and introduction claim that DNNs are 'only capable' of generalizing to orientations resembling in-plane rotations. The heatmaps and correlations support a tendency, but do not establish this exclusivity. Quantify recognition inside and outside explicitly defined small-angle/in-plane regions, or narrow the claim to the dominant pattern observed in these synthetic instance-classification experiments. Section 7's acknowledgment of other possible settings is helpful but does not resolve the stronger headline claim.

Necessary evaluation clarification: Section 4 fits the model parameters by maximizing the same Pearson correlation subsequently reported, without describing an independent evaluation split. These results establish descriptive fit rather than independently validated prediction. Either evaluate fitted parameters on held-out data or consistently present the model as descriptive. Moreover, correlations are often only approximately 0.2–0.4 for the shifted/union orientation distributions in Figure 4c, and AE sometimes performs worse than an individual component, including in the fourth column. Section 6's characterization of AE as ultimately best needs correction and discussion of these limitations.

Necessary experimental detail: Appendix B specifies 200K images but does not adequately describe independent training, validation, and test-set construction or test-set sizes. Per-cubelet sample counts and treatment of empty or sparsely populated bins are also unspecified, making the reliability of the orientation maps difficult to assess. Since learning rates were selected using OoD stability, clarify whether that selection used data separate from final evaluation.

Necessary model-specification clarification: With the sigmoid and parameter ordering printed in Section 4, the stated grid has b >= 1 while its inputs lie in [0,1], implying that every predicted value is at most 0.5. This contradicts the explanation that the sigmoid can match near-unit accuracies. Although this does not itself invalidate Pearson correlations, the implemented parameter ranges and fitting procedure need an accurate, reproducible description.

Optional improvements: Additional cross-category trials would strengthen the result currently based on one trial. A sensitivity check using Haar-uniform rotations would help establish how much the findings depend on uniform Euler-angle sampling, which weights physical orientations unevenly. Neither extension requires a new architecture or state-of-the-art recognition performance.
